FPMC adds long-term user–item affinity to a factorized transition from the last item (or averaged over the last basket). Separate source/target embeddings allow asymmetric transitions: A→B need not equal B→A. Standard FPMC has neither multi-lag exponential weighting nor a sigmoid mixing gate. [FPMC paper](https://www.ra.ethz.ch/cdstore/www2010/www/p811.pdf). FOSSIL replaces explicit user preference vectors with a normalized sum of historical item embeddings, then adds weighted transitions from the last L items. Each lag has a global plus user-specific learned coefficient; weights need not decay monotonically or lie in [0,1]. It shares source/target embedding tables across long- and short-term components while keeping source and target roles distinct. [FOSSIL paper, equations 5–8](https://arxiv.org/html/1609.09152).

A proposed SASRec score s(H,j)=s_SASRec(H,j)+g(H)Σ[k=1..5]w_k〈a_last-k,b_j〉, with normalized exponential w_k and sigmoid g, therefore reuses established additive preference/transition modeling. Its distinguishing choices are the SASRec backbone, constrained decay, and—if context-dependent—adaptive gating. SASRec already models recent and longer-range dependencies; its contribution should not be described as purely long-term. These comparisons establish close precedent, not proof of novelty.

Suggested ablations: recency—last-one versus uniform-five versus exponential-five versus learned lag weights, keeping residual normalization fixed; directionality—unrestricted T versus (T+Tᵀ)/2 using the same factor tables, since tying embeddings also reduces capacity; gating—gate=1, tuned constant, learned global sigmoid, context-dependent sigmoid; capacity—SASRec alone and parameter-matched wider SASRec or an auxiliary prediction head without explicit transitions. Include residual-only and SASRec-plus-ungated-transition controls. Hold splits, seeds, negatives, loss and training budget fixed; select by the prescribed four-category macro validation HR@10.
